newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian banks seen benefiting from savings plan.
newsitem.headline: Australian banks seen benefiting from savings plan.

text.p: Australian banks are seen benefiting from the government's proposal in its 1997/98 budget for a 15 percent tax rebate on earnings from savings, analysts said.
"It's obviously going to be a benefit for the banks," said Riccardo Briganti, senior economist of strategy at Macquarie Equities.
But Don Argus, the managing director at National Australia Bank Ltd, said the proposal would not necessarily help banks over other financial institutions.
"I don't (think it will benefit banks), I think there is a group of people this is aimed at that probably don't invest in shares," Argus told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.

Hans Kunnen, group economist at Colonial State Bank, said: "It won't be superannuation funds, they have already got their concession. So yes, I guess it benefits non-superannuation financial institutions where people put their savings."

The savings tax rebate, which is estimated to cost A$2.04 billion a year by 2000/01 (July/June), would be introduced in two stages, with a 7.5 percent rebate applying from July 1, 1998 and the full rebate from July 1, 1999.
